boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented University of Oklahoma rituals, campus lore, and game-day traditions.

cards.title: Sooner Magic
cards.subtitle: A rallying cry beyond the field
cards.notes: Use the phrase as OU frames it: a reminder to prepare, persist, and keep working when a result looks unlikely.
cards.short_summary: A football-era phrase adopted across OU life.
cards.evidence_claim: OU says Barry Switzer coined “Sooner Magic” for comeback football victories and that it was later adopted across athletics, academics, and research.
cards.access_notes: A campus phrase; no special access is required to learn about it.

cards.title: Touch the Champion Sign
cards.subtitle: Owen Field pregame ritual
cards.notes: Look for the historic locker-room message and its meaning before a game; treat it as a team ritual rather than a visitor activity.
cards.short_summary: Players touch a longstanding pregame sign.
cards.evidence_claim: OU states that Bud Wilkinson placed the sign in the locker room in the late 1940s and that every Sooner player still touches it before going onto Owen Field.
cards.access_notes: The ritual is associated with the football team’s locker-room route; do not seek restricted access.

cards.title: Walk Around the Clock Tower
cards.subtitle: A campus graduation myth
cards.notes: Photograph the Clock Tower from the surrounding walkways, then decide whether to follow the campus lore and avoid passing beneath it.
cards.evidence_claim: OU documents the campus myth that walking underneath the Clock Tower means a student will not graduate within the standard four-year period.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow posted campus access rules.

cards.title: Sit at the Spoonholder
cards.subtitle: North Oval campus lore
cards.notes: Find the Spoonholder on the North Oval and read the Class of 1910 memorial story alongside its later campus-courtship myth.
cards.short_summary: A rebuilt class memorial with a marriage-lore story.
cards.evidence_claim: OU says the Spoonholder began as a Class of 1910 memorial, was rebuilt by the Class of 1999, and carries a myth that a kiss there foretells marriage.
cards.access_notes: Located on the North Oval lawn; view respectfully and follow campus rules.

cards.entity_name: Turning of the OU Ring at Commencement
cards.title: Turn the OU Ring Outward
cards.subtitle: From student to graduate
cards.notes: If participating in the Ring Ceremony, note the inward-facing OU logo; at commencement, graduates are invited to turn it outward.
cards.short_summary: OU marks graduation with a symbolic ring turn.
cards.evidence_claim: OU says ring recipients wear the logo inward after the Ring Ceremony and are asked at commencement to turn it outward as they leave OU.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires an OU class ring and the relevant ceremony; observing public ceremony details may vary.

cards.entity_name: Pride of Oklahoma interlocking OU and “go-go”
cards.title: Watch the Interlocking OU
cards.subtitle: Pride of Oklahoma game-day formation
cards.notes: At a football game, watch for the Pride’s interlocking-OU formation and the opening “go-go” while “Boomer Sooner” is played.
cards.short_summary: A marching-band formation tied to the fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: OU’s history page identifies the Pride’s first “go-go” and marching of the interlocking “OU” while playing “Boomer Sooner” as a defining game-day element.
cards.access_notes: Typically experienced during football game programming; event entry policies apply.

cards.title: See the Sooner Schooner Run
cards.subtitle: Owen Field after OU scores
cards.notes: Watch for the covered wagon and its white ponies after an OU score, and leave driving and animal handling to the designated spirit squads.
cards.short_summary: A covered wagon makes a score-following ride.
cards.evidence_claim: OU says the Sooner Schooner races across Owen Field after every OU score, pulled by matching white ponies named Boomer and Sooner.
cards.access_notes: View from authorized stadium seating or public event areas; do not approach the horses or wagon.

cards.entity_name: The OU Chant and raised finger
cards.title: Raise One Finger for the Chant
cards.subtitle: A unity gesture during “Oklahoma”
cards.notes: During the OU Chant, follow the documented gesture: stand and raise one finger, then join only if you know the words and setting.
cards.short_summary: The chant pairs lyrics with a raised-finger gesture.
cards.evidence_claim: OU states that students, student-athletes, alumni, and fans are encouraged to stand and raise one finger during the Chant as a symbol of unity.
cards.access_notes: A public school-spirit practice; follow the etiquette and instructions of the event.

cards.title: Learn the Original Yell
cards.subtitle: A chant adopted after OU’s first football season
cards.notes: Recognize the “Hi rickety whoop-te-do” lines as the university’s documented yell, not simply a generic fight-song refrain.
cards.short_summary: OU’s early football culture produced the “Boomer Sooner” yell.
cards.evidence_claim: OU says students formulated and adopted the yell in fall 1895 after the first football game and first oratorical contest made a yell necessary.
cards.access_notes: A public school-spirit practice; participate appropriately for the event.

cards.entity_name: Pride of Oklahoma Drum Major Strut
cards.title: Spot the Drum Major’s Strut
cards.subtitle: A distinctive Pride of Oklahoma movement
cards.notes: During a Pride performance, watch the drum major’s practiced back-bending field movement, formally known within the band as “the strut.”
cards.short_summary: The band’s drum major performs a named marching movement.
cards.evidence_claim: OU identifies the Pride of Oklahoma drum major’s distinctive game-day movement as “the strut” and describes it as a Sooner tradition.
cards.source_title: 7 Things You (Maybe) Don’t Know About the Pride of Oklahoma | The University of Oklahoma
cards.access_notes: Watch during authorized band appearances; the movement is performed by trained drum majors.
